title: Azure RBAC Scopes and Roles
description: Explore how RBAC scopes work and choose the right built-in or custom role for your scenario.

data.text: Scope in RBAC determines the boundary where a role assignment is effective. Think of it like layers of an onion — the narrower the scope, the more secure your permissions.

data.title: RBAC Scope Hierarchy
items: Management group — applies to multiple subscriptions
Subscription — applies to everything in a subscription
Resource group — applies to one resource group
Resource — applies to a single resource like a storage account

data.title: View All Role Assignments at Subscription Scope
data.content: Use Azure CLI to list every role assignment in a subscription.

data.title: Create a Custom Role with JSON
data.content: Define a custom role that allows reading blobs but not modifying them.
data.code:
{
  "Name": "Blob Reader Only",
  "IsCustom": true,
  "Description": "Read blobs without write access.",
  "Actions": [
    "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers/read",
    "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/generateUserDelegationKey/action"
  ],
  "NotActions": [],
  "DataActions": [
    "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers/blobs/read"
  ],
  "AssignableScopes": ["/subscriptions/{subscription-id}"]
}

data.title: Scope Exploration
data.description: Create a role assignment at the resource group scope, then verify it applies only to resources inside that group.
steps: Assign the Reader role to your user at the resource group scope.
Try to list storage accounts in a different resource group.
data.expectedOutcome: You can read resources in 'scoped-rg' but cannot see resources in other groups.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Scope is hierarchical: management group > subscription > resource group > resource.
Use the narrowest scope that still works.
Custom roles let you fine-tune permissions when built-in roles are too broad.
